subject: CloudGrid EU invoices misroute — recovery & credit allocation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudGrid: EU invoices misrouted to legacy entity — recovery plan

Hi team,

Quick heads-up: during the Sept bill run we discovered ~€142,450 of EU customer invoices that were posted to the legacy UK entity (RGD-UK-001) instead of the EMEA operating entity (RGD-EU-01). The affected invoices are for CloudGrid (see attached entity_mapping.csv) — they applied payment to the legacy entity which triggered incorrect VAT tagging and left our AR ageing skewed for the EMEA books.

Impact summary (prelim):
- AR misstatement in EMEA for Sep: ~€142.45k (invoices 20412–20437)
- Taxes: VAT posted to legacy entity returns; potential refund/credit step needed from CloudGrid to avoid double VAT reporting
- Cash: CloudGrid already remitted a lump payment that cleared the legacy entity ledger (remittance PDF attached)

Ask: Laura — can your team draft the reversing journal to move the gross invoice amounts into the correct AR buckets and a second JV to record the inter-entity clearing? Marcus — I need the recommended VAT clearing lines and whether we should post a contra-credit or a manual VAT refund accrual. Grace — please surface whether this hits any revenue recognition windows for Sept (are these performance obligations already recognized?).

Timeline: we need a practical remediation plan to present to CloudGrid this week (target sign-off by Tue 2026-10-06). I attached a journal_template.xlsx to speed approvals.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CloudGrid: EU invoices misrouted to legacy entity — recovery plan

Karthik — thanks, saw this. I pulled the source invoices and remittance; attaching entity_mapping.csv and the proposed journal_template.xlsx (see tab "CG_recovery").

Prelim journal approach (for review) — two-step:
1) Reverse entries posted to legacy entity (RGD-UK-001):
   - DR Sales Revenue 142,450 EUR
   - CR AR (legacy) 142,450 EUR
   - Memo: Reverse misapplied invoices 20412–20437
2) Re-post to correct entity (RGD-EU-01) as AR balances and re-recognize VAT:
   - DR AR (RGD-EU-01) 142,450 EUR
   - CR Sales Revenue 120,000 EUR
   - CR VAT Payable 22,450 EUR
   - Memo: Re-posted invoices with corrected tax jurisdiction

VAT handling: Marcus — I left a placeholder VAT clearing line to move VAT cost between entities (intercompany VAT clearing). If CloudGrid will accept a credit memo for the VAT portion, we can issue an AR credit (reducing gross AR) and offset with an intercompany payable; otherwise we may need to book a temporary VAT accrual until refunded.

Revenue recognition: Grace — based on the invoice meta I'm seeing most of these were billed for SaaS subscriptions covering Oct–Dec 2026 (deferred revenue). If so, the reversal/repost won't affect recognized revenue for Sep; just balance sheet movements. Please confirm.

Next steps:
- Marcus to confirm VAT lines and signing authority
- Grace to confirm rev rec impact by EOD Fri 2026-10-02
- Karthik to draft client communication with the proposed credit/memo treatment

Laura
Accounting Manager — Revenue
Redwood Inference

Attachments: entity_mapping.csv; journal_template.xlsx

From: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@cloudgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: cloudgrid-payments@cloudgrid.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:43:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CloudGrid: EU invoices misrouted to legacy entity — recovery plan

Thanks for flagging and for sending the attachments — appreciate the fast turnaround.

A few clarifications from our side:
- We initiated a bulk payment on 2026-09-28 for €150,000 which appears to have been applied to the UK legacy entity (we have remittance CG_Remittance_Sept2026.pdf attached).
- CloudGrid's AP policy prefers a client-facing credit memo (not a refund) for tax adjustments; we will accept a single credit memo that offsets VAT exposure on our books, provided the memo references the original invoice numbers.
- We have compliance constraints in Germany: any VAT reallocation must be evidenced by corrected invoice/credit documentation.

We're agreeable to the proposed two-step internal journal adjustment so long as Redwood issues a credit memo for the VAT component and confirms the net AR balance on RGD-EU-01 after re-posting. Would also like visibility into the timing — we need the credit memo before our Oct 15 VAT filing.

I'll stand by for the formal credit memo draft and the signed mutual action plan.

Best,
Amelia Hart
Head of Finance Operations
CloudGrid Inc.

Attachment: CG_Remittance_Sept2026.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Hart <amelia.hart@cloudgrid.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CloudGrid: EU invoices misrouted to legacy entity — recovery plan

Amelia — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming CloudGrid's preference. Confirming Redwood proposal and timeline below: 

Agreed remediation & timeline (mutual action plan):
1) Internal accounting — reversal + repost (Redwood) — complete by 2026-10-09 EOD
   - Laura/Accounting to post reversing and re-posting JVs (using journal_template.xlsx).
2) Client documentation — Redwood to issue one credit memo (VAT portion) referencing invoices 20412–20437 — draft to CloudGrid by 2026-10-07
3) Client confirmation — CloudGrid to confirm acceptance and post on their side by 2026-10-12 
4) VAT filing window — we will ensure credit memo delivery before CloudGrid's Oct 15 filing; Redwood tax will provide signed evidence if needed.

Marcus — please confirm the VAT clearing entry below so we can include it in the draft memo:
   - DR VAT Receivable (RGD-UK-001) 22,450 EUR
   - CR Intercompany VAT Clearing 22,450 EUR

Grace — quick note: if any portion of these invoices recognized revenue in Sept, we will create offsetting deferred entries; otherwise the profiles look deferred and you should be able to leave revenue deferral intact — let us know by EOD.

Amelia — attaching the draft credit memo (in journal_template.xlsx tab "CreditMemoDraft"). If that looks good I will route for signature and post the reversing journals.

Thanks everyone — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
